sub: NCCGA Regional 3, Nov 14-15 2026 · Driver 275/300 · 2-wood 265/280 · 4-wood 255/270 at 70°F · club and aim re-solved for the wind and temperature at each hole
tee_hour_source: golfer 2026-11-13: Saturday tee time 10:36 am Central, starting on 1 (he thinks), Back tees, Drop rule. tee_hour = Saturday (also the calm-day book's temperatures: 42 F on 1 to 48.5 F on 18, was 35-47 at 9:00); tee_hours = [Saturday, Sunday] defaults of the page's Tee time slider: Sunday's time is not known and stays 9:00. 2026-11-13 evening: the par-5 Second shot tables (opt/par5_second.py World.wx, par5_menu) and the par-3 targets (opt/par3_target.py TEE_HOURS) now read tee_hours per day and were re-solved on the Friday-evening forecast (NWS hourly, fetched 23:08 UTC).

climate.source: mid-November normals for St. Louis (lows ~38 F, highs ~57 F, prevailing SSW wind ~10 mph)

foot: Tee sets: Back (6,623, 72.4/133) is the set the NCCGA played here in 2024 (6,623; Nov 2025 used a 6,377 combo); Middle (6,154) is fully solved from its own boxes; The Tips, Champions and Forward move the Back tee along the line. The tee sheet is not posted: check each tee plaque and use Move this tee to match it (tee shots are solved every 20 yds; par 3s move in 5-yd steps). Calm-day picks: 256 prior draws per hole; the wind grids at the card tee are refined on 16,000 common swings per club. Clubs: Driver to Mid iron plus an 8-iron (162 carry, assumed ~12-yd gapping below the 210 long iron). A tee ball on or by a green is scored with putts (drivable 10). The map was checked on NAIP 2023 (0.3 m, colour infrared), NAIP 2022 and the 2014 3DEP lidar, and re-checked hole by hole on Nov 9. Photos: USDA NAIP 2023-08-19.

1.Back: Why Driver: 76% fairway; the 2-wood finds 3 points more fairway but leaves 20 yds more.

2.Back: Why Driver: the same 76% fairway as the 2-wood and 20 yds closer.

3.Back: Why Driver: a par 5 with nothing gained by laying back; the left-centre line keeps the right side out of play.

5.Back: Why Driver: a 452-yd hole where every yard counts: 20 yds closer than the 2-wood.

6.Back: Why Driver: 79% fairway into the widest part of the hole.

8.Back: Why Driver down the left: it shortens the hole; the 2-wood leaves 20 yds more.

9.Back: Why Driver, narrowly: it gets 20-30 yds closer, but only half the balls find fairway; the 2-wood and 4-wood find more fairway and are almost as good.

10.Back: Why: a wood at the left half of the green. Miss left of the flag, not right. About 7 balls in 8 finish on or around the green; an iron to the right fairway instead costs about 0.4 strokes.
10.Middle: Why: 4-wood at the left half of the green. Miss left of the flag, not right. About 9 balls in 10 finish on or around the green; an iron to the right fairway instead costs about 0.3 strokes.

11.Back: Why Driver, narrowly: it leaves about 30 yds less; the 4-wood is straighter (71% fairway against 58%).

13.Back: Why Driver: a par 5 with 70% fairway; nothing in reach that a shorter club avoids.

15.Back: Why Driver: it carries the trouble at 250 yds that the shorter woods land in, and gets 24 yds closer than the 2-wood.

16.Back: Why 4-wood: it stops at the mouth of the narrow part (77% fairway); the Driver runs through the fairway half the time and the 2-wood a quarter of the time.

18.Back: Why Driver: a par 5 with nothing in reach that a shorter club avoids.

physics.source: 2026-11-13 second pass, second_pass/PHYSICS.md (independent trajectory model fitted to the TrackMan tour tables): the engine's 0.00075 / F is the air alone; a ball at air temperature adds ~0.0004 / F (about 1 % of ball speed at 45 F) and the weekend's 1027-1031 hPa high another ~0.0002 / F equivalent between 38 and 52 F -> 0.00135; crosswind drift 1.5 yds per mph for every full shot (was 1.14 for the driver, 0.8 for a mid iron); head / tail multipliers for the shorter clubs (mid iron 1.65: -9 % of carry into 10 mph)

engine.native_penalty_area_source: golfer's ground truth 2026-11-13: 'All of the native grass is penalty area generally if it is that height - no finding it, too thick and tall.' Every standing tall-native zone is priced by the engine's water rule (the ball is gone from the first yard in: one stroke + a shot from rough at the point where it crossed the edge) instead of the depth-ramp lost-ball model (25 % lost at the edge rising to 65 %, stroke and distance). 16's short-grass mound stays its penal-lie class; mown areas stay rough. Hole 10: the whole band between the ditch and the right-hand fairway is staked penalty area (his drawing), mapped as water in trace.py LATE['10'].

tall_grass_alt.source: golfer 2026-11-13: the tall grass may be played as a lost ball (re-tee) instead of a one-stroke drop; he decides on the day. Second rule set, solved separately (truth/v2_lost, truth_middle/v2_lost; fastsolve run.py --tall-grass lost) and switched on the page; never the default. A ball finishing in a tall-grass zone costs one stroke and the same shot again (closed form, v2_course.lost_ball_ev). Mapped water and ditches stay one stroke + drop. (also_ll, hole 10's band beside the right fairway, removed 2026-11-13 afternoon: the band is mown rough and no longer in the map.)

par5_second_source: 2026-11-13, golfer request: go for the green or lay up on the par 5s, and where (opt/par5_second.py, opt/par5_page.py, PAR5.md). Clubs off the deck (DECK in par5_second.py): no Driver or 2-wood; 4-wood 255 carry / 270 total, the golfer's own number (Nov 13: "4-wood same as off tee"; the first build took 15 off), long iron 210, mid iron 185, 8-iron 162, 9-iron 150, PW 138, GW 126, SW 113; from rough 4 % shorter, 25 % wider, no 4-wood. Patterns since the Nov 13 data pass (second_pass/FAIRWAY_WOOD_DATA.md, DECK_SETS 'central'): every club's width and distance window x 1.75 = PGA Tour proximity by yardage x 1.5 club for club (a scratch amateur's pattern, Arccos / Stagner), which reproduces the engine's amateur table within 0.06 strokes from 115-167 yds; the first build used the tee patterns (Tour-level). The tee-pick re-check (pill) is on the central pattern for holes 3 and 6 in Drop mode, kept from the first build elsewhere; the hole 10 lay-up table is not re-solved
par3_targets_source: 2026-11-13: the DECADE edge rule as a constraint (5 % of the plays-like number from every part of the green edge, +3 toward a penalty edge, +2 trees / greenside bunker, +1 a bunker 5-10 yds off; lesser of two evils when it does not fit), best expected strokes inside it (PAR3.md section 0, opt/par3_decade.py; model opt/par3_target.py with penalty balls priced at the crossing point); written for every tee set; the file also carries the outline the margins are measured on and the four edge distances the page prints
par3_bag_source: 70-F stock carries of the par-3 model (opt/par3_target.py bag; 4-iron = the engine's 210 long iron, 6-iron = the 185 mid iron; 5-, 7-, 9-iron, PW, GW, SW, LW assumed ~12-yd gapping)
approach_pattern_source: 2026-11-14 late, golfer: 'why 79 yards wide with a 220-yard shot? wouldn't that be a lot more narrow?', then on the first split (x 1.25, 230 shot 62 wide): 'a 230-yard shot should only be planned for like a 40 or 50-yard dispersion'. The single x 1.75 (deck) / x 1.5 (par-3 tee) on width AND distance window drew a 220-yd shot wider in yds than his Driver. Proximity data cannot tell sideways error from distance error and no published split by handicap was found, so the sideways half is the golfer's own planning width = the tee pattern x 1.0 (long iron 43, 230 shot 48, 4-wood 54 yds at 95 %: the tee table's iron rows), off the fairway and on par-3 tees; all of the gap to a scratch amateur's proximity is distance (second_pass/FAIRWAY_WOOD_DATA.md 'Sideways and distance apart', PAR3.md section 9): off the fairway the distance window x 2.25, slight mishits 12 % (sand wedge) rising to 32 % (4-wood) at 85-95 % of the carry, bad ones 2.5 -> 6 %; par-3 tee x 1.75 / 12 -> 22 % / 2.5 -> 4 %. Flat-green proximity stays within 5 ft of the scratch level (Tour x 1.5 club for club). opt/par5_second.py DECK_SETS central and opt/par3_target.py read it; P5_DECK_SET=central_175 and P3_PATTERN_MULT=1.5 give the single-multiplier runs. par3_pattern_mult is kept for that override only
par3_pattern_source: 2026-11-14 check against published data (PAR3.md section 8, second_pass/FAIRWAY_WOOD_DATA.md): the par-3 solver's iron patterns were Tour-level (flat 15-yd-radius green: 92 % of greens and 25 ft from 135, 80-83 % and 31-33 ft from 180, 75 % and 36 ft from 200; Tour proximity 24 / 34 / 42 ft). Width and distance window of every par-3 club x 1.5 (a tee is a perfect lie: the low end of the 1.5-1.75 used off the deck) gives 75 % / 36 ft, 56-60 % / 44-47 ft, 46-51 % / 50-54 ft = Tour x 1.4-1.5, a scratch amateur. opt/par3_target.py reads it (P3_PATTERN_MULT overrides); targets and ladder of both rule sets re-solved on it
par3_drift_source: second_pass/PHYSICS.md 2b: every full iron drifts 1.4-1.5 yds per crosswind mph (flight time 6.3-7 s); the page had no crosswind allowance on par 3s
temp_note: air, a ball at air temperature and this weekend's high pressure
